lines.text: Your dog has no idea where you go when you leave the house.
It does know how long you've been gone.
The second you leave, your smell starts fading from every room.
One dog scientist thinks they read that fade like a clock.
Strong smell, you just left. Faint smell, you're late.
One dog on the BBC always went to wait just before his owner got home.
Then they waved the owner's sweaty T-shirt around the room.
The dog didn't move. His nose said the owner just left.
Swedish researchers left dogs alone for thirty minutes, two hours, or four.
After the longer waits, the welcome home was way bigger.
So your dog knows when you're late.
It still has no idea where you go when you leave the house.
